stories.title: Hiranyakashipu's quest for power
stories.story: Hiranyakashipu performed severe austerities seeking extraordinary protection and power, eventually becoming convinced that his strength made him nearly invincible.
stories.teaching: Power gained without humility can turn ambition into destructive pride.

stories.title: Prahlada remains devoted
stories.story: Prahlada remained devoted to Vishnu despite pressure from his father Hiranyakashipu to abandon his faith.
stories.teaching: Strong conviction can remain steady even when powerful people demand conformity.

stories.title: Hiranyakashipu and Prahlada
stories.story: Hiranyakashipu's authority could not force Prahlada to abandon his convictions, revealing the limits of worldly power over inner belief.
stories.teaching: External authority cannot fully control a person's inner convictions.

stories.title: Hiranyaksha challenges the gods
stories.story: Hiranyaksha used his immense strength to challenge divine powers and disturb the balance of the worlds.
stories.teaching: Strength becomes destructive when it is used to dominate rather than protect.

stories.title: Hiranyaksha and Varaha
stories.story: Hiranyaksha confronted Varaha after disrupting the cosmic order, ultimately losing the conflict.
stories.teaching: Unchecked power can eventually meet consequences when it disrupts the larger order.

stories.title: Mahishasura's rise
stories.story: Mahishasura gained great power and used it to challenge the gods and establish his authority over the heavenly realm.
stories.teaching: Ambition without restraint can transform leadership into domination.

stories.title: Mahishasura and Durga
stories.story: Mahishasura's growing power and refusal to yield led to his confrontation with Durga.
stories.teaching: Pride can make a powerful person underestimate consequences.

stories.title: Bhasmasura's boon
stories.story: Bhasmasura obtained a powerful boon and immediately sought to use it for his own advantage.
stories.teaching: A powerful ability guided only by desire can become dangerous to everyone, including its owner.

stories.title: Bhasmasura is deceived by his own desire
stories.story: Bhasmasura's desire for power led him into a situation where his own actions turned against him.
stories.teaching: Unchecked desire can make a person vulnerable to their own impulses.

stories.title: Ravana's ambition
stories.story: Ravana accumulated great knowledge, strength, and authority, but his ambition and desires increasingly shaped his decisions.
stories.teaching: Knowledge and strength do not prevent destructive choices when desire dominates judgment.

stories.title: Ravana and Sita
stories.story: Ravana's desire for Sita led him to abduct her, creating a conflict that ultimately brought destruction upon his kingdom.
stories.teaching: Desire that ignores another person's autonomy can lead to severe consequences.

stories.title: Kumbhakarna's counsel
stories.story: Kumbhakarna recognized problems in Ravana's actions but remained connected to his brother and fought alongside him.
stories.teaching: Loyalty can conflict with judgment, and difficult choices require recognizing both.

stories.title: Vibhishana leaves Ravana
stories.story: Vibhishana advised Ravana to return Sita and avoid war. When Ravana rejected the counsel, Vibhishana left Lanka.
stories.teaching: Integrity may require opposing even those to whom we are loyal.

stories.title: Bali's generosity
stories.story: King Bali was known for generosity and kept his commitment when Vamana asked for three steps of land, despite the consequences.
stories.teaching: Keeping a promise can require accepting personal sacrifice.

stories.title: Bali and Vamana
stories.story: Bali possessed great authority but ultimately accepted Vamana's claim and surrendered what he had promised.
stories.teaching: True character can be revealed when a powerful person accepts the consequences of a promise.

stories.title: Andhaka's desire
stories.story: Andhaka's desire and attachment led him into conflict with Shiva and the forces protecting Parvati.
stories.teaching: Uncontrolled desire can distort judgment and create destructive conflict.

stories.title: Tripurasura's cities
stories.story: The three sons of Tarakasura built powerful cities and became formidable forces whose growing power threatened the balance of the worlds.
stories.teaching: Accumulated power becomes dangerous when it is used without restraint.

stories.title: Tarakasura's boon
stories.story: Tarakasura sought protection through austerities and used the resulting power to challenge the gods.
stories.teaching: Strategic pursuit of power can become destructive when its purpose is domination.

stories.title: Shumbha's demand
stories.story: Shumbha sought to possess the divine power represented by Devi and demanded submission rather than accepting her independence.
stories.teaching: Treating another being as property turns desire into domination.

stories.title: Nishumbha's attachment
stories.story: Nishumbha stood beside Shumbha and pursued the same desire for possession and dominance.
stories.teaching: Attachment to possession can strengthen ego and make wise judgment difficult.

stories.title: Raktabija's multiplying power
stories.story: Raktabija possessed a power by which drops of his blood could produce additional forms like himself, making him difficult to defeat.
stories.teaching: A problem can multiply when every attempt to confront it creates more of the same problem.

stories.title: Madhu and Kaitabha
stories.story: Madhu and Kaitabha became powerful opponents and challenged the cosmic order before ultimately being defeated through divine strategy.
stories.teaching: Strength alone is not enough when opponents can use strategy and circumstance.

stories.title: Duryodhana's jealousy
stories.story: Duryodhana's jealousy toward the Pandavas influenced his decisions and contributed to escalating conflict.
stories.teaching: Jealousy can turn competition into destructive attachment and conflict.

stories.title: Duryodhana refuses compromise
stories.story: Duryodhana rejected attempts at compromise and remained unwilling to give the Pandavas even a small share of territory.
stories.teaching: Pride and unwillingness to compromise can turn disagreement into irreversible conflict.

stories.title: The Asura perspective
stories.story: Across many stories, powerful figures pursue desire, status, protection, wealth, or authority. Their choices reveal how ambition and self-interest can shape moral decisions.
stories.teaching: Understanding selfish desire is important because recognizing its influence can prevent it from controlling one's choices.
